title: सप्तविंशतितमोऽध्यायः

summary.en: Sanjaya praises Yudhishthira's devotion to dharma and argues that it would be better for him to live by begging than to win a kingdom by slaughtering his kin. Life is short, he says, and anger and desire lead to ruin; if the Kurus will not give back the kingdom, the Pandavas should rather renounce it.
summary.kn: ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರನ ಧರ್ಮನಿಷ್ಠೆಯನ್ನು ಹೊಗಳಿ, ಬಂಧುಗಳನ್ನು ಕೊಂದು ರಾಜ್ಯ ಗೆಲ್ಲುವುದಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಭಿಕ್ಷೆ ಬೇಡಿ ಬದುಕುವುದು ಮೇಲು ಎಂದು ಸಂಜಯನು ವಾದಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಜೀವನ ಅಲ್ಪ, ಕೋಪ ಕಾಮಗಳು ವಿನಾಶಕ್ಕೆ ಒಯ್ಯುತ್ತವೆ; ಕುರುಗಳು ರಾಜ್ಯ ಮರಳಿಸದಿದ್ದರೆ ಪಾಂಡವರು ಅದನ್ನು ತ್ಯಜಿಸುವುದೇ ಲೇಸು ಎನ್ನುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: सञ्जय युधिष्ठिर की धर्मनिष्ठा की प्रशंसा कर तर्क देते हैं कि बन्धुओं का वध कर राज्य जीतने से भिक्षा माँगकर जीना श्रेष्ठ है। वे कहते हैं कि जीवन अल्प है, क्रोध और काम विनाश की ओर ले जाते हैं; यदि कुरु राज्य न लौटाएँ तो पाण्डवों को उसका त्याग ही कर देना चाहिए।
summary.te: యుధిష్ఠిరుని ధర్మనిష్ఠను కొనియాడి, బంధువులను చంపి రాజ్యం గెలవడం కంటే భిక్షాటనతో జీవించడం మేలని సంజయుడు వాదిస్తాడు. జీవితం స్వల్పమని, కోపం, కామం వినాశానికి దారితీస్తాయని, కురువులు రాజ్యం తిరిగి ఇవ్వకపోతే పాండవులు దానిని త్యజించడమే మేలని అంటాడు.
summary.ta: யுதிஷ்டிரரின் அறப்பற்றைப் புகழ்ந்து, உறவினரைக் கொன்று அரசை வெல்வதைவிட இரந்து வாழ்வதே மேல் என்று ஸஞ்ஜயன் வாதிடுகிறான். வாழ்க்கை குறுகியது, சினமும் ஆசையும் அழிவுக்கு இட்டுச் செல்லும்; குருக்கள் அரசைத் திருப்பித் தராவிட்டால் பாண்டவர்கள் அதைத் துறப்பதே நல்லது என்கிறான்.
summary.ml: യുധിഷ്ഠിരന്റെ ധർമ്മനിഷ്ഠയെ സഞ്ജയൻ പ്രശംസിക്കുന്നു; ബന്ധുക്കളെ കൊന്ന് രാജ്യം നേടുന്നതിനേക്കാൾ യാചിച്ചു ജീവിക്കുന്നതാണ് നല്ലതെന്ന് അദ്ദേഹം വാദിക്കുന്നു. ജീവിതം ചെറുതാണെന്നും, കോപവും ആഗ്രഹവും നാശത്തിലേക്ക് നയിക്കുമെന്നും അദ്ദേഹം പറയുന്നു; കുരുക്കൾ രാജ്യം തിരികെ നൽകുന്നില്ലെങ്കിൽ പാണ്ഡവർ അത് ഉപേക്ഷിക്കുകയാണ് നല്ലതെന്ന് ഉപദേശിക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 5.27; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Tue Jan 23 2024

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
धर्मे नित्या पाण्डव ते विचेष्टा
लोके श्रुता दृश्यते चापि पार्थ ।
महास्रावं जीवितं चाप्यनित्यं
संपश्य त्वं पाण्डव मा विनीनशः ॥

meaning.en: Your efforts, Pandava, are always for dharma, famed in the world and seen too, Partha; life is a great leak and impermanent; see this, Pandava, and do not be destroyed.

verses.text:
न चेद्भागं कुरवोऽन्यत्र युद्धा-
त्प्रयच्छन्ते तुभ्यमजातशत्रो ।
भैक्षचर्यामन्धकवृष्णिराज्ये
श्रेयो मन्ये न तु युद्धेन राज्यम् ॥

meaning.en: If the Kurus do not give you your share except by war, O one without enemies, I think it better to live by begging in the kingdom of the Andhakas and Vrishnis than to have a kingdom by war.

verses.text:
अल्पकालं जीवितं यन्मनुष्ये
महास्रावं नित्यदुःखं चलं च ।
भूयश्च तद्वयसो नानुरूपं
तस्मात्पापं पाण्डव मा प्रसार्षीः ॥

meaning.en: The life of man is short, a great leak, ever painful and unstable, and it does not match one's years; so, Pandava, do not spread sin.

verses.text:
कामा मनुष्यं प्रसजन्त एव
धर्मस्य ये विघ्नमूलं नरेन्द्र ।
पूर्वं नरस्तान्धृतिमान्विनिघ्नँ-
ल्लोके प्रशंसां लभतेऽनवद्याम् ॥

meaning.en: Desires cling to a man, king, and are the root of obstruction to dharma; the man who first steadily slays them wins faultless praise in the world.

verses.text:
निबन्धनी ह्यर्थतृष्णेह पार्थ
तामेषतो बाध्यते धर्म एव ।
धर्मं तु यः प्रवृणीते स बुद्धः
कामे गृद्धो हीयतेऽर्थानुरोधात् ॥

meaning.en: Craving for wealth is a bond here, Partha; and in pursuing it dharma is hurt. He who chooses dharma is wise; one greedy for desire is ruined by the pursuit of wealth.

verses.text:
धर्मं कृत्वा कर्मणां तात मुख्यं
महाप्रतापः सवितेव भाति ।
हानेन धर्मस्य महीमपीमां
लब्ध्वा नरः सीदति पापबुद्धिः ॥

meaning.en: Having made dharma the chief of actions, one shines with great power like the sun; a man of sinful mind who loses dharma, even winning this earth, sinks.

verses.text:
वेदोऽधीतश्चरितं ब्रह्मचर्यं
यज्ञैरिष्टं ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च दत्तम् ।
परं स्थानं मन्यमानेन भूय
आत्मा दत्तो वर्षपूगं सुखेभ्यः ॥

meaning.en: One who has studied the Veda, practiced chastity, sacrificed, given to Brahmins, and thinking of the highest state has for a long span of years given up pleasures,

verses.text:
सुखप्रिये सेवमानोऽतिवेलं
योगाभ्यासे यो न करोति कर्म ।
वित्तक्षये हीनसुखोऽतिवेलं
दुःखं शेते कामवेगप्रणुन्नः ॥

meaning.en: but who, fond of pleasure, indulges too much and does not practice yoga, after his wealth is gone, deprived of pleasure, lies in great pain, driven by the force of desire.

verses.text:
एवं पुनरर्थचर्याप्रसक्तो
हित्वा धर्मं यः प्रकरोत्यधर्मम् ।
अश्रद्दधत्परलोकाय मूढो
हित्वा देहं तप्यते प्रेत्य मन्दः ॥

meaning.en: Likewise one who is fully engaged in pursuing wealth, abandons dharma and does wrong, a deluded fool with no faith in the other world, grieves after death when he leaves the body.

verses.text:
न कर्मणां विप्रणाशोऽस्त्यमुत्र
पुण्यानां वाप्यथ वा पापकानाम् ।
पूर्वं कर्तुर्गच्छति पुण्यपापं
पश्चात्त्वेतदनुयात्येव कर्ता ॥

meaning.en: Neither of good nor of bad actions is there destruction in the next world; the merit or sin goes first to the doer, and afterwards the doer follows it.

verses.text:
न्यायोपेतं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो यदन्नं
श्रद्धापूतं गन्धरसोपपन्नम् ।
अन्वाहार्येषूत्तमदक्षिणेषु
तथारूपं कर्म विख्यायते ते ॥

meaning.en: The food you give to Brahmins in accordance with right, purified by faith, rich in scent and taste, and the best fees at offerings to ancestors, such is the deed reported of you.

verses.text:
इह क्षेत्रे क्रियते पार्थ कार्यं
न वै किंचिद्विद्यते प्रेत्य कार्यम् ।
कृतं त्वया पारलोक्यं च कार्यं
पुण्यं महत्सद्भिरनुप्रशस्तम् ॥

meaning.en: In this field, Partha, work is done; there is no work to be done after death. You have done the work for the other world, great merit praised by the good.

verses.text:
जहाति मृत्युं च जरां भयं च
न क्षुत्पिपासे मनसश्चाप्रियाणि ।
न कर्तव्यं विद्यते तत्र किंचि-
दन्यत्र वै इन्द्रियप्रीणनार्थात् ॥

meaning.en: One leaves death, old age and fear, and hunger, thirst and the mind's unpleasantness; there nothing needs to be done except what pleases the senses.

verses.text:
एवंरूपं कर्मफलं नरेन्द्र
मात्रावता हृदयस्य प्रियेण ।
स क्रोधजं पाण्डव हर्षजं च
लोकावुभौ मा प्रहासीश्चिराय ॥

meaning.en: Such is the fruit of action, king, for one who is moderate and dear to the heart. Pandava, do not forsake for long both worlds, the one born of anger and the one born of joy.

verses.text:
अन्तं गत्वा कर्मणां या प्रशंसा
सत्यं दमश्चार्जवमानृशंस्यम् ।
अश्वमेधो राजसूयस्तथेष्टः
पापस्यान्तं कर्मणो मा पुनर्गाः ॥

meaning.en: The praise that comes at the end of actions is truth, self-control, honesty and non-cruelty; having performed the Ashvamedha and Rajasuya, do not go back to the end of a sinful act.

verses.text:
तच्चेदेवं देशरूपेण पार्थाः
करिष्यध्वं कर्म पापं चिराय ।
निवसध्वं वर्षपूगान्वनेषु
दुःखं वासं पाण्डवा धर्महेतोः ॥

meaning.en: If you, Parthas, carry out this sinful deed in this way for a long time, you will have to live many years in the forests, a sorrowful life, for dharma's sake.

verses.text:
अप्रव्रज्ये योजयित्वा पुरस्ता-
दात्माधीनं यद्बलं ते तदासीत् ।
नित्यं पाञ्चालाः सचिवास्तवेमे
जनार्दनो युयुधानश्च वीरः ॥

meaning.en: Having earlier set your strength to non-exile, that strength of yours was in your own hands; these Panchalas are always your ministers, and Janardana and the hero Yuyudhana,

verses.text:
मत्स्यो राजा रुक्मरथः सपुत्रः
प्रहारिभिः सह पुत्रैर्विराटः ।
राजानश्च ये विजिताः पुरस्ता-
त्त्वामेव ते संश्रयेयुः समस्ताः ॥

meaning.en: the Matsya king, golden-chariot Virata with his sons and his striking sons, and the kings you conquered before would all take refuge in you.

verses.text:
महासहायः प्रतपन्बलस्थः
पुरस्कृतो वासुदेवार्जुनाभ्याम् ।
वरान्हनिष्यन्द्विषतो रङ्गमध्ये
व्यनेष्यथा धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दर्पम् ॥

meaning.en: With great allies, blazing, standing on strength, honored by Vasudeva and Arjuna, killing the best of your enemies in the arena you would crush the pride of Dhritarashtra's son.

verses.text:
बलं कस्माद्वर्धयित्वा परस्य
निजान्कस्मात्कर्शयित्वा सहायान् ।
निरुष्य कस्माद्वर्षपूगान्वनेषु
युयुत्ससे पाण्डव हीनकालम् ॥

meaning.en: Why, after strengthening the enemy's force and weakening your own allies and having lived many years in the forests, do you now, Pandava, want to fight at an inopportune time?

verses.text:
अप्रज्ञो वा पाण्डव युध्यमानो
अधर्मज्ञो वा भूतिपथाद्व्यपैति ।
प्रज्ञावान्वा बुध्यमानोऽपि धर्मं
संरम्भाद्वा सोऽपि भूतेरपैति ॥

meaning.en: A fool who fights, or one ignorant of dharma, falls from the road to prosperity; or one wise who knows dharma falls too, from anger.

verses.text:
नाधर्मे ते धीयते पार्थ बुद्धि-
र्न संरम्भात्कर्म चकर्थ पापम् ।
अद्धा किं तत्कारणं यस्य हेतोः
प्रज्ञाविरुद्धं कर्म चिकीर्षसीदम् ॥

meaning.en: Your mind, Partha, is not set on unrighteousness, and you have not done sinful deeds out of rage; so truly what is the reason that you want to do this deed against your wisdom?

verses.text:
अव्याधिजं कटुकं शीर्षरोगं
यशोमुषं पापफलोदयं च ।
सतां पेयं यन्न पिबन्त्यसन्तो
मन्युं महाराज पिब प्रशाम्य ॥

meaning.en: Anger, not born of disease, bitter, a headache, destroyer of fame, with sinful fruit, is a drink the good drink and the wicked do not; drink it, great king, and be calm.

verses.text:
पापानुबन्धं को नु तं कामयेत
क्षमैव ते ज्यायसी नोत भोगाः ।
यत्र भीष्मः शांतनवो हतः स्या-
द्यत्र द्रोणः सहपुत्रो हतः स्यात् ॥

meaning.en: Who would desire what leads to sin? Patience is better for you than enjoyments, when Bhishma, son of Shantanu, might be slain, or Drona with his son might be slain,

verses.text:
कृपः शल्यः सौमदत्तिर्विकर्णो
विविंशतिः कर्णदुर्योधनौ च ।
एतान्हत्वा कीदृशं तत्सुखं स्या-
द्यद्विन्देथास्तदनुब्रूहि पार्थ ॥

meaning.en: Kripa, Shalya, Somadatta's son, Vikarna, Vivimshati, Karna and Duryodhana; what happiness would there be, having killed them? Tell me what you would find, Partha.

verses.text:
लब्ध्वापीमां पृथिवीं सागरान्तां
जरामृत्यू नैव हि त्वं प्रजह्याः ।
प्रियाप्रिये सुखदुःखे च राज-
न्नेवं विद्वान्नैव युद्धं कुरुष्व ॥

meaning.en: Even having won this earth to its ocean borders, you would not escape old age and death, or pleasant and unpleasant, pleasure and pain, king; knowing this, do not fight.

verses.text:
अमात्यानां यदि कामस्य हेतो-
रेवंयुक्तं कर्म चिकीर्षसि त्वम् ।
अपाक्रमेः संप्रदाय स्वमेभ्यो
मा गास्त्वं वै देवयानात्पथोऽद्य ॥

meaning.en: If, for the sake of your ministers' desire, you want to do such a deed, then give them their own and withdraw; do not today leave the path leading to the gods.
